subject: How do I correctly scale a formative latent variable?

messages.author: c3a661560c1fc010
messages.subject: How do I correctly scale a formative latent variable?
parts:
Dear list,

apologies for the simplicity of my question and ignorance. I was wondering how one scales a formative latent variable? I know that one option is to multiply one indicator by 1. What I do not understand is that if depending on which indicator is multiplied the direction of the path coefficient will change.

If I do something like this:

latent<~1*a+b+c

I will get a positive path coefficient for the latent variable.

whereas if I do something like this:

latent<~a+b+1*c

I will get a negative path coefficient.

I guess this maybe related to the nature of the relationship between the individual indicators and the response variable of interest, some could have a positive effect and others could have a negative effect. Any help would be greatly appreciated!

Best wishes,

Antonio

messages.author: 671b14edc9322fa7
messages.subject: Re: How do I correctly scale a formative latent variable?
parts:
Hi

You are doing it correctly.

If you regress latent on a, b, c and the coefficients of a and c are of different sign, then constraining a coefficient that was originally negative to be 1 (positive) will reverse the sign. The same happens if you have a reverse coded indicator (negative loading) and constrain that to be 1 (positive).

Mikko

thanks again,

Yes. If you expect the coefficient to be negative, then you can scale with -1.

Mikko
